document:
Exercise: Standing Dumbbell Upright Row

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- external_rotation
- shoulder_abduction

Primary Muscles:

- traps

Secondary Muscles:

- biceps
- shoulders

Equipment:

- dumbbell

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- shoulder_strength
- upper_back_development

Contraindications:

- condition: shoulder instability, reason: The exercise may exacerbate shoulder instability due to the overhead nature and potential for excessive force on the rotator cuff muscles.
- condition: rotator cuff injury, reason: The exercise places significant stress on the rotator cuff, which could worsen an existing injury.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Dumbbell Upright Row - Alternating Arms, instructions: ['Grasp a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated (palms forward) grip that is slightly less than shoulder width. The dumbbells should be resting on top of your thighs. Your arms should be extended with a slight bend at the elbows and your back should be straight. This will be your starting position.', 'Use your side shoulders to lift one dumbbell as you exhale, then switch to the other arm. The dumbbells should be close to the body as you move it up and the elbows should drive the motion. Continue to lift them until they nearly touch your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the dumbbells, your elbows should always be higher than your forearms. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.', 'Lower the dumbbells back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.', 'Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.']

Substitution Options:

- name: Barbell Upright Row, equipment: barbell

Instructions:

- Grasp a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated (palms forward) grip that is slightly less than shoulder width. The dumbbells should be resting on top of your thighs. Your arms should be extended with a slight bend at the elbows and your back should be straight. This will be your starting position.
- Use your side shoulders to lift the dumbbells as you exhale. The dumbbells should be close to the body as you move it up and the elbows should drive the motion. Continue to lift them until they nearly touch your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the dumbbells, your elbows should always be higher than your forearms. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
- Lower the dumbbells back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
